ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a rectangular field $ABCD$ has the ratio of its length $AB$ to its width $BC$ as $\sqrt{2} : 1$. $DE \perp AC$, and $BF \perp AC$, with the perpendicular feet being points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Now, there is a plan to plant flowers and grass in the quadrilateral region $DEBF$. What is the ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to the area of the rectangle $ABCD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
$ \therefore AD\parallel BC$, $AD=BC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$ \therefore \angle DAE=\angle BCF$.\\
Since $BF\perp AC$, $DE\perp AC$,\\
$ \therefore \angle AED=\angle CFB=90^\circ$, $BF\parallel DE$.\\
In $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CBF$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DAE=\angle BCF\\
\angle AED=\angle CFB\\
AD=CB
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$ \therefore \triangle ADE \cong \triangle CBF$ (AAS),\\
$ \therefore DE=BF$, $AE=CF$,\\
Since $BF\parallel DE$,\\
$ \therefore $ Quadrilateral $DEBF$ is a parallelogram,\\
Let $AD=BC=x$, then $CD=AB=\sqrt{2}x$,\\
$ \therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2}x)^2+x^2}=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
Since $DE\perp AC$ at point $E$,\\
$ \therefore S_{\triangle ADC}=\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot DE$,\\
$ \therefore x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{3}x\cdot DE$,\\
$ \therefore DE=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x$,\\
In $\triangle ADE$, $AE=\sqrt{x^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$ \therefore EF=AC-AE-CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$ \therefore S_{\text{quadrilateral }DEBF}=EF\cdot DE=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}x^2$,\\
Since $S_{\text{rectangle }ABCD}=x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{2}x^2$,\\
$ \therefore $ The ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to rectangle $ABCD$ is $\boxed{1\colon 3}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, a rectangular field $ABCD$ has the ratio of its length $AB$ to its width $BC$ as $\sqrt{2}:1$. $DE \perp AC$ and $BF \perp AC$, with perpendicular feet at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Find the ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to the area of rectangle $ABCD$.
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore AD\parallel BC$, $AD=BC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DAE=\angle BCF$.\\
Since $BF\perp AC$, $DE\perp AC$,\\
$\therefore \angle AED=\angle CFB=90^\circ$, $BF\parallel DE$.\\
In $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CBF$,\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\angle DAE=\angle BCF\\
\angle AED=\angle CFB\\
AD=CB
\end{array}\right.$,\\
$\therefore \triangle ADE \cong \triangle CBF$ (AAS),\\
$\therefore DE=BF$, $AE=CF$,\\
Since $BF\parallel DE$,\\
$\therefore$ quadrilateral $DEBF$ is a parallelogram,\\
Let $AD=BC=x$, then $CD=AB=\sqrt{2}x$,\\
$\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2}x)^2+x^2}=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
Since $DE\perp AC$ at point $E$,\\
$\therefore S_{\triangle ADC}=\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot DE$,\\
$\therefore x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{3}x\cdot DE$,\\
$\therefore DE=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x$,\\
In $\triangle ADE$, $AE=\sqrt{x^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$\therefore EF=AC-AE-CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\
$\therefore S_{\text{quadrilateral }DEBF}=EF\cdot DE=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}x^2$,\\
Since $S_{\text{rectangle }ABCD}=x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{2}x^2$,\\
$\therefore$ the ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to rectangle $ABCD$ is $\boxed{1\colon 3}$.

The projection parameter of point D onto line AC is (D·v)/(v·v)=1/3, so E=(1/3)v=(√2/3,1/3). The projection parameter of point B onto line AC is (B·v)/(v·v)=2/3, so F=(2/3)v=(2√2/3,2/3).

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, a rectangular field $ABCD$ has the ratio of its length $AB$ to its width $BC$ as $\sqrt{2}:1$. $DE \perp AC$ and $BF \perp AC$, with perpendicular feet at points $E$ and $F$, respectively. Find the ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to the area of rectangle $ABCD$.
ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is a rectangle,\\ $\therefore AD\parallel BC$, $AD=BC$, $\angle ABC=90^\circ$,\\ $\therefore \angle DAE=\angle BCF$.\\ Since $BF\perp AC$, $DE\perp AC$,\\ $\therefore \angle AED=\angle CFB=90^\circ$, $BF\parallel DE$.\\ In $\triangle ADE$ and $\triangle CBF$,\\ $\left\{\begin{array}{l} \angle DAE=\angle BCF\\ \angle AED=\angle CFB\\ AD=CB \end{array}\right.$,\\ $\therefore \triangle ADE \cong \triangle CBF$ (AAS),\\ $\therefore DE=BF$, $AE=CF$,\\ Since $BF\parallel DE$,\\ $\therefore$ quadrilateral $DEBF$ is a parallelogram,\\ Let $AD=BC=x$, then $CD=AB=\sqrt{2}x$,\\ $\therefore AC=\sqrt{AB^2+BC^2}=\sqrt{(\sqrt{2}x)^2+x^2}=\sqrt{3}x$,\\ Since $DE\perp AC$ at point $E$,\\ $\therefore S_{\triangle ADC}=\frac{1}{2}AD\cdot CD=\frac{1}{2}AC\cdot DE$,\\ $\therefore x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{3}x\cdot DE$,\\ $\therefore DE=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x$,\\ In $\triangle ADE$, $AE=\sqrt{x^2-\left(\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x\right)^2}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\ $CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\ $\therefore EF=AC-AE-CF=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x$,\\ $\therefore S_{\text{quadrilateral }DEBF}=EF\cdot DE=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}x\cdot \frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}x=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}x^2$,\\ Since $S_{\text{rectangle }ABCD}=x\cdot \sqrt{2}x=\sqrt{2}x^2$,\\ $\therefore$ the ratio of the area of quadrilateral $DEBF$ to rectangle $ABCD$ is $\boxed{1\colon 3}$.

Image description: In the figure there is a rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left, B at the lower right, C at the upper right, and D at the upper left; diagonal AC connects from A to C. Points E and F are both on AC, and drawing a perpendicular from D to AC gives foot E, drawing a perpendicular from B to AC gives foot F; the corresponding DE and BF are drawn in the figure.

Reasoning: According to the specified coordinate method, let A=(0,0), B=(√2,0), C=(√2,1), D=(0,1), so AB:BC=√2:1. The direction vector of diagonal AC is v=(√2,1), and |v|^2=2+1=3. The projection parameter of point D onto line AC is (D·v)/(v·v)=1/3, so E=(1/3)v=(√2/3,1/3). The projection parameter of point B onto line AC is (B·v)/(v·v)=2/3, so F=(2/3)v=(2√2/3,2/3).

Calculate the area of quadrilateral D-E-B-F. Using the shoelace formula according to vertices D(0,1), E(√2/3,1/3), B(√2,0), F(2√2/3,2/3): the forward sum is 0+0+√2·(2/3)+(2√2/3)·1=4√2/3; the reverse sum is 1·(√2/3)+(1/3)·√2+0+0=2√2/3. Therefore the area is (1/2)(4√2/3-2√2/3)=√2/3. The area of rectangle ABCD is √2·1=√2, so the area ratio is (√2/3)/√2=1/3, namely 1:3.
